- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 70.0), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +2.0% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to catch upward momentum; add 0.5–1.0% bias toward higher end of forecast range.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% upward bias to end of forecast if sentiment swings from negative to positive.
- If sentiment is flat or mildly negative (avg -0.1 to 0.0), model often misses upward trend; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to avoid underprediction.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.4) and recent price is >70.0; if so, add 0.5% downward bias to prevent overcorrection.
